The best-performing design (index 7) shows improved forward pitch and capture margin but still exhibits intermittent backward falls and insufficient forward velocity. counterfactual.purpose: Test whether reducing torso mass lowers COM height, improves pitch and capture margin, and increases walking seeds.

new_hypotheses.causal_chain: High torso_mass → ↑ COM height & pitch inertia → ↓ hip pitch torque effectiveness → backward pitch (negative pitch_mean) → COM behind CoP (negative com_ahead_of_cop) → capture point outside support (negative capture_margin) → increased flight and falls (both forward due to compensatory stepping and backward due to insufficient recovery).
new_hypotheses.mechanism: Torso mass is at its maximum allowed value, raising the overall centre of mass and increasing the pitch inertia. This makes it difficult for the hip actuators to produce sufficient forward pitch torque to counteract the natural backward tendency caused by the high COM, resulting in a backward lean, premature foot placement, and capture point falling outside the support interval.

parsed.result_reading: The robot fails to walk on all 4 seeds (n_walking=0, n_fell=4). Falls are split: 2 forward, 2 backward, with median fall time 6.98 s (range 1.0–8.0 s). While upright, the robot shows a backward torso lean (pitch_mean = ‑0.102 rad, healthy range 0.01–0.115 rad) and a negative pitch rate (pitch_rate_mean = ‑0.342 rad/s, healthy ≈0). The centre of mass is excessively high (com_height_over_L_mean = 0.974, healthy 0.646–0.94) and lies behind the centre of pressure (com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean = ‑0.060, healthy ‑0.001–0.011). Consequently the capture point is outside the support interval (capture_margin_over_L_mean = ‑0.234, healthy ‑0.169–0.009). Flight fraction is too high (0.027 vs healthy 0.004–0.007), indicating insufficient ground contact for balance. Torque saturation is notable at the knee (saturation_frac_knee = 0.0053, healthy ≈0) while hip and ankle saturation are negligible. Friction utilisation is within limits but slightly elevated (p95 = 0.40 vs healthy 0.17–0.34). Step frequency is normal (3.41 Hz, healthy 2.57–3.88) but step length is short (step_length_over_L = 0.132 vs healthy 0.157–0.231). These symptoms point to a combination of excessive upper‑body mass raising the COM and reducing the ability to generate corrective hip torque, leading to backward leans and inadequate capture‑point regulation.

parsed.result_reading: Initial observation O0 showed 0/4 seeds walking, all fell (2 forward, 2 backward). Key symptoms: backward lean (pitch_mean -0.102 rad), COM height high (0.974 L), capture point far behind support (capture_margin -0.234 L), low forward speed (com_vx_mean 0.057 m/s), high flight fraction, high friction utilisation. After counterfactual E1 (torso_mass@x0.5), walking increased to 2/4, falls to 2/4 (both backward). COM height decreased to 0.852 L, capture_margin improved to -0.187 L, but pitch_mean became more negative (-0.145 rad) and pitch_rate_end strongly negative (-0.985 rad/s), indicating increased backward pitch acceleration. Forward speed dropped sharply (com_vx_mean 0.0025 m/s, com_vx_end -0.265 m/s). Knee saturation and max friction utilisation decreased.

Hip pre‑fall saturation appeared (0.030) while knee pre‑fall saturation vanished. Pitch mean became less negative (‑0.073 vs ‑0.102); pitch rate mean less negative (‑0.060 vs ‑0.342). parsed.result_reading:
The latest experiment was E4 (balance_gain@x0.7). After decreasing balance gain to 93.1 (0.7×133), the robot still walked 0 of 4 seeds; n_fell remained 4. Median fall time increased to 5.93 s (up from 4.08 s) and time_upright decreased to 3.56 s (down from 4.08 s). COM velocity at the end became slightly forward (0.010 m/s) and capture‑margin end moved slightly more negative (‑0.053). Pre‑fall hip saturation rose to 0.055 while knee saturation dropped to 0.0. No other quantities changed beyond tolerance. Thus reducing balance gain slightly extended upright time but did not restore walking.

Recall that only E1 (torso_mass@x0.5) yielded any improvement: walking seeds rose from 0 to 2, time_upright increased to 5.62 s, capture margin improved (‑0.187 vs ‑0.234), COM height lowered, and pre‑fall knee saturation fell from 0.045 to 0.020, with max friction utilisation dropping from 1.0 to 0.62. All other trials (E2, E3, E4) produced zero walking seeds.

conclude.explanation: After exhaustive testing of torso mass, torque limit, foot length, and hip amplitude, the robot still fails to achieve consistent walking. The best-performing design (index 7) shows improved forward pitch and capture margin but still exhibits intermittent backward falls and insufficient forward velocity. Given the remaining budget and the lack of promising alternative hypotheses, we conclude that further experimentation is unlikely to yield a design that passes hidden verification. The submitted design is the current best (index 7) from the torso_mass repair.

parsed.result_reading: Latest experiments: E6 (torso_mass@x0.7 & torque_limit@x1.5 on design 7) increased walking seeds from 2 to 3. Torso mass decreased (~9.5), torque limit increased (~43.5). Pitch mean increased (more forward lean), capture margin over L mean increased (from -0.221 to -0.119), time upright increased (5.63 → 10.0 s), pre-fall saturation fraction knee showed no change. E7 (foot_length@x1.5 & hip_amp@x1.5 on design 7) decreased walking seeds from 2 to 0. Foot length doubled (~0.161 m) and hip amplitude increased (~0.095 rad). Pitch mean increased (more forward lean) but step length over L decreased (0.139 → 0.087), time upright decreased (5.63 → 1.80 s), capture margin over L end worsened (-0.484 → -0.637), com_vx mean showed no significant change.
